compliance.verdict: No blocking defect: gbf-test-07 is a correct, solvable and fair item that passes every gate and every compliance check, with one medium and three low findings. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on a scratch copy (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-07/task_copy) so the task's own gates.json was not touched. The result matches the author's gates.json exactly: 10/10 reference runs pass, 272 tokens, 3/3 variants pass, the start graph fails first at V6 (f2p fails, p2p passes), and 12/12 mutants are valid and all 12 are killed. The compliance checks are clean. Running build.py in a scratch copy rebuilt all six files byte-for-byte. schemas.validate reports no errors. The canary GUID is only in task.json. The reference and start chains both hash to test. The licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (false for a composed chain) and disjointness fields follow the rules. id, folder and split agree, and the level is L1 with 5 functional blocks. The instruction's description of the start signal is accurate: the start output alternates between -0.2 and +0.2 every 16 samples, with mean 0 and RMS 0.2. The oracle accepted every plausible correct design I ran through the real ladder or simulated: low_pass_2 at 40 dB, Kaiser windows at the 40 dB beta, the Low Pass Filter block with a Hann window, and equiripple filters with 0.1 dB ripple. It rejected the rectangular and Bartlett windows, which fail the 40 dB requirement, as it should. The open issues are: (1) the item nearly duplicates gbf-test-01 and belongs to a four-item group of square-to-sine low-pass items, which the cluster_id rule does not group together; (2) the stopband sentence in spec_properties claims more than the reference achieves; (3) the 5 % passband and 0.01 mean tolerances are not stated in the instruction; (4) the oracle accepts a wide range of cutoff and width values, not just 2.5 kHz and 1 kHz.

findings.claim: gbf-test-07 nearly duplicates gbf-test-01 and is one of four square-wave-to-sine low-pass items in the 19-item test split. The cluster_id-by-signature rule puts these related items in four different clusters, while putting test-07 in the same cluster as the unrelated gbf-test-11. Clustered standard errors and the cluster bootstrap would therefore count dependent items as independent.
findings.evidence: gbf-test-01 (build): '1.5 kHz square wave ... sample rate of 48 kHz ... Low-pass filter it so that only the 1.5 kHz fundamental remains'; its reference uses a Low Pass Filter with cutoff 3000 and width 1000. gbf-test-07 (modify): a 1.5 kHz square at 48 kHz, add a low-pass with cutoff 2500 and width 1000 to get a sine. The same theme appears in gbf-test-08 (repair, 1.2 kHz square at 48 kHz to sine) and gbf-test-12 (tune, 1 kHz square clock at 32 kHz to sine). Their cluster_ids are four different chain signatures. gbf-test-07 has the same cluster_id as gbf-test-11 (chain:analog_sig_source_x|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|low_pass_filter|blocks_add_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink), which is a DAC tone retune at 24 kHz. Eval plan line 221: 'Items from the same question family or source flowgraph are not independent, so we use clustered standard errors'. The slot brief only asked to 'insert a filtering or scaling stage with stated parameters'.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-theme test-07 within its slot brief so it is not the 1.5 kHz / 48 kHz square-to-sine task again. Options: insert a scaling or DC-removal stage, use a high-pass to remove hum, or use a different source, frequency and rate. Otherwise add a family-level cluster (for example 'family:square_to_sine_lpf') shared by test-01, -07, -08 and -12, and flag the duplication on the team review sheet.

findings.claim: spec_properties says that 'everything at or above 3 kHz ... is attenuated by at least 40 dB'. That is false for the reference and for all three variants. The oracle measures something narrower: the combined power of the harmonics at 4.5 kHz and above. Read strictly, with GNU Radio's convention that the stopband starts at cutoff + width/2 = 3 kHz, the golden reference does not meet the instruction's 'at least 40 dB of stopband attenuation'. The stated 23.4 % harmonic share is also the continuous-time value.
findings.evidence: Responses computed with firdes: the reference Hamming design (115 taps) gives H(3000 Hz) = -27.4 dB and only stays at or below -40 dB from about 3129 Hz. The variants give -20.7 dB (Hann), -30.0 dB (Blackman) and -33.3 dB (low_pass_2 at 60 dB) at 3 kHz. The square wave has no energy between 1.5 and 4.5 kHz, so band_fraction over [3000, 24000] only measures harmonic suppression. For the discrete 32-samples-per-period square wave, the harmonic share relative to the fundamental is 0.2298, not pi^2/8 - 1 = 0.2337. The measured start band fraction, 0.1868 = 0.2298/1.2298, agrees with 0.2298. The threshold is therefore about 0.07 dB more lenient than stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the stopband entry in spec_properties to: 'the square wave's odd harmonics (4.5 kHz and above) together are at least 40 dB below their unfiltered level, measured as their share of the output power'. Note that GNU Radio's window-design transition width is nominal. Optionally change the instruction to 'at least 40 dB attenuation of the square wave's harmonics (4.5 kHz and up)' so the reference meets the literal wording.

findings.claim: The instruction does not state the oracle's tolerances (output RMS ±5 %, mean ±0.01, tone ±15 Hz). Related items (test-01, test-12) do state theirs. A filter that meets every stated design number but has 1 dB of passband ripple fails two checks. One of them is the p2p 'offset' check, which only fails because the filter sits before the Add Const block.
findings.evidence: Real-ladder run of the reference with the low-pass replaced by fir_filter_xxx, taps 'optfir.low_pass(1, samp_rate, 2000, 3000, 1.0, 40)', plus an Import block. This design has its transition from 2 to 3 kHz (cutoff 2.5 kHz, width 1 kHz) and about 40 dB stopband. Result: V6 fails with passband gain RMS 0.191098 > 0.18907 and offset mean 0.014063 > 0.01; the stopband share of 1.3e-5 passes. The same design with 0.1 dB ripple passes (RMS 0.179626, mean 0.001). Placing the 1 dB design after the Add Const would pass the mean check, because its input has no DC there, but would still fail RMS. scipy.remez with 69 taps (peak stopband -40.2 dB, +0.74 dB at 1.5 kHz) also fails RMS (0.19644).
findings.suggested_fix: State the tolerance in the instruction, for example 'a passband gain of 1 (within 5 %, i.e. at most about 0.4 dB of passband ripple)', and optionally the expected output level ('a sine of about 0.255 peak, RMS 0.180 within 5 %'). Alternatively, record in spec_properties that the offset check also limits the filter's DC gain to within 5 % when the filter comes before the Add Const.

findings.claim: The oracle enforces the stated cutoff (2.5 kHz) and transition width (1 kHz) only loosely. Filters that clearly contradict the instruction still pass, and the mutation set only tests changes large enough to be caught.
findings.evidence: I ran firdes.low_pass designs (Hamming) on the exact 0/0.5 × 0.8 - 0.2 square wave through oracles.evaluate with this task's checks. With width 1000, every cutoff from 2000 to 3800 Hz passes. With cutoff 2500, every width from 100 to 2000 Hz passes; for example, cutoff 3500 with width 1000, and cutoff 2500 with width 2000, both pass. The task's mutants only use cutoff ×2 or ×0.5, width ×6, and samp_rate 96000, all outside this range. This follows from the probe signal, which has energy only at 1.5 kHz and at 4.5 kHz and above.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a spec_properties note that the cutoff and width are checked only through their effect on the 1.5 kHz fundamental and on the harmonics at 4.5 kHz and above (cutoff roughly 2-3.8 kHz accepted). Alternatively, phrase the filter request in outcome terms (pass 1.5 kHz at unity gain, suppress 4.5 kHz and above by 40 dB) so the instruction does not state numbers the oracle cannot check. Optionally add a mutant near the edge of the accepted range, such as cutoff ×1.6, to document where the boundary is.

item-quality.verdict: The item is solvable and I found no realistic correct solution that the oracle rejects. The reference passes, and so do Low Pass Filter blocks with Hamming, Hann, Blackman, Kaiser or Blackman-Harris windows, interp_fir_filter_fff, firdes.low_pass_2 at 40/50/60 dB, optfir equiripple designs with 0.1-0.5 dB ripple (under both band-edge readings), and an elliptic IIR in iir_filter_xxx (ladder run). The start graph fails only f2p at V6, as designed. The item still does not survive review, because the oracle is much looser than the instruction. It accepts filters designed for 25 dB stopband attenuation (40 dB is required) and filters with the wrong cutoff (3.5 kHz instead of 2.5 kHz). spec_properties describes a 3 kHz / 40 dB stopband property that the reference itself does not meet. The scenario also nearly duplicates gbf-test-01 in the same test split. I recommend revision before team sign-off: tighten or reword the stopband requirement, be honest about which filter numbers are verified, and change the theme or numbers. I did not edit the task. findings.claim: The f2p 'stopband' check does not enforce the stated 'at least 40 dB of stopband attenuation'. Filters with only about 21-36 dB stopband attenuation pass V6. The first spec_properties entry ('everything at or above 3 kHz ... is attenuated by at least 40 dB') is false for the reference filter itself and is not what the oracle measures.
findings.evidence: The check is band_fraction over 3000-24000 Hz with max 2.337e-5. That is a power-weighted total over the square wave's harmonics at 4.5, 7.5, ... kHz, so it says nothing about 3-4.5 kHz. Because the 4.5 kHz harmonic dominates, the check accepts about 37 dB there. Real ladder runs (./gb ladder --task items/tier_f/test/gbf-test-07/task.json): (1) a FIR filter with taps firdes.low_pass_2(1, samp_rate, 2500, 1000, 25, window.WIN_KAISER, 1.33) plus an Import block, i.e. a filter explicitly designed for 25 dB, passes V6 with stopband 2.3e-5, rms 0.1837 (file w1_lowpass2_25dB_kaiser.grc). (2) A Low Pass Filter block with win=WIN_KAISER, beta=2.0 passes V6 with stopband 1.1e-5 (w3_kaiser_beta2_block.grc). Its worst attenuation is 21.0 dB for f >= 3 kHz and 36.2 dB for f >= 4 kHz. Frequency responses from GNU Radio's firdes (resp.py, resp2.py): the reference Hamming filter (115 taps) gives only 27.4 dB at 3000 Hz, and 57.1 dB only from 3.5 kHz upward. The 30 dB Kaiser low_pass_2 also passes the oracle. A minor point: the threshold uses the continuous-time harmonic share pi^2/8-1 = 23.37 %, but the sampled 32-sample square wave has 22.97 %.
findings.suggested_fix: State the requirement in measurable terms, e.g. 'the square wave's harmonics (4.5 kHz and above) must end up at least 40 dB below the 1.5 kHz sine'. Add a per-harmonic check on the 4.5 kHz component, e.g. band_fraction lo=4400, hi=4600, max of about 1.14e-5, which is (sin(pi/32)/sin(3pi/32))^2 * 1e-4 for the sampled wave. That check rejects the 25 dB and beta=2 designs. Rewrite the first spec_properties entry so it does not claim 40 dB from 3 kHz. Alternatively, drop the '40 dB' figure: the Low Pass Filter block has no attenuation parameter, and the oracle cannot verify it at the stopband edge.

findings.claim: The two numbers the modify instruction is built around, cutoff 2.5 kHz and transition width 1 kHz, are effectively unchecked. The square wave has no energy between 1.5 and 4.5 kHz, so any low-pass that passes 1.5 kHz and suppresses 4.5 kHz and above gets full credit. A model that misreads or ignores the stated parameters is scored as correct. The 12 mutants only use gross factors (x2, x0.5, x6), which hides this.
findings.evidence: Real ladder: a Low Pass Filter block with cutoff_freq 3500 and width 1000 passes V6 with stopband 0.0, rms 0.1805, peak 1500 Hz, mean 0 (w2_cutoff_3500.grc). Simulation with GNU Radio firdes taps and the task's own oracles.evaluate (sim.py) also passes: cutoff 2000/width 1000, 3000/1000, 3800/1000, 4000/500, 1800/500, 2500/100 and 2500/2000. Only 2500/3000 fails. spec_properties never says the cutoff and width are only bounded to roughly 1.8-4 kHz and up to about 2 kHz.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the requirement behavioural (unity gain at 1.5 kHz plus harmonic suppression as in F1) and present cutoff and width as suggested design values, noting in spec_properties that they are not individually verified, or change the test signal so the band edges matter (for example, a square-wave frequency or extra probe tone whose components sit just inside the 2 kHz passband edge and just beyond the 3 kHz stopband edge). Add near-miss mutants such as cutoff 3.5 kHz and width 2 kHz to document what the oracle can and cannot detect.

findings.claim: gbf-test-07 nearly duplicates gbf-test-01 in the same test split, and 4 of the 19 test items are 'turn a square wave into a sine with a low-pass filter'. The chain-signature cluster_id puts this item in the same cluster as an unrelated item (gbf-test-11) and in a different cluster from its real twin (gbf-test-01), so the clustered intervals in eval plan §'Uncertainty' do not cover the redundancy.
findings.evidence: gbf-test-01 (build, L1) instruction: '1.5 kHz square wave ... 48 kHz ... Low-pass filter it so that only the 1.5 kHz fundamental remains: its harmonics (4.5 kHz, 7.5 kHz and so on) must be removed ...'. gbf-test-07 uses the same 1.5 kHz square wave, 48 kHz rate, the same low_pass_filter and the same 4.5/7.5 kHz harmonic oracle, with cluster chain:...|low_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink in test-01 vs ...|low_pass_filter|blocks_add_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink here. gbf-test-08 (repair: square to 1.2 kHz sine) and gbf-test-12 (tune: square-wave clock to sine) are the same theme. gbf-test-11 (retune a cosine tone at 24 kHz) has exactly this item's cluster_id. The eval plan says 'Items from the same question family or source flowgraph are not independent, so we use clustered standard errors'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the theme of gbf-test-07 to another insertion, e.g. a high-pass/DC-removal stage on an offset tone, a band-pass on a two-tone signal, or a pure scaling stage. If the theme stays, change the numbers away from test-01's 1.5 kHz / 48 kHz and give the square-to-sine items (test-01/07/08/12) a shared scenario-level cluster key for the clustered statistics.

findings.claim: The instruction says 'a passband gain of 1' with no tolerance, while the oracle allows ±5 % in RMS and ±0.01 in mean. A standard equiripple design with 1 dB passband ripple (and 40 dB stopband) is rejected, and it also fails the p2p mean check when placed at the source. It is arguable whether that design meets 'gain 1'.
findings.evidence: sim.py: optfir.low_pass(1, 48000, 2000, 3000, 1.0, 40) (71 taps) gives rms 0.1906, i.e. +5.8 % against the 0.1801 ± 5 % expectation, so f2p fails. Placed before the multiply, its mean is 0.0141 > 0.01, so p2p fails. The 2500/3500 edge version gives rms 0.1685, which also fails. The same designs with 0.1 or 0.5 dB ripple pass.
findings.suggested_fix: State the tolerance in the instruction, e.g. 'a passband gain of 1 (within 5 %)' or 'at most 0.4 dB of passband ripple', so an equiripple designer knows the ripple budget.

findings.claim: The L1 label sits on the boundary of the proposal's level definition. The proposal lists 'filtering' as an L2 characteristic, and this item's whole content is designing and inserting a filter to a 40 dB spec, though it has only 5 functional blocks.
findings.evidence: Methodology_Proposal_to_7Dec.txt line 83: 'L1 (≤ 5 blocks, single-rate chain), L2 (6–15 blocks, rate changes, modulation/demodulation, filtering)'. The reference has 5 functional blocks (src, scale, lpf, shift, out) at a single rate, so L1 by block count, which matches the computed rule and the set's convention (test-01/08/10/11/12 also put filters in L1).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep L1 but record in review notes that L1 counts blocks only and filtering alone does not raise the level, so the team applies one consistent reading across all items.
